title: Rigging for Rescue
description: U.S. Marines and Sailors with Mountain Warfare Training Center (MWTC) participate in a Rigging for Rescue ropework course on MWTC, Bridgeport, Calif., May 6 – 10, 2019. The course was held to better prepare mountain warfare instructors with the abilities to conduct a safe training environment. (U.S. Marine Corps video by MAGTFTC COMMSTRAT)
keywords: Palms, Mountain Warfare Training Center, MWTC, MAGTFTC, Center MCAGCC, Cpl Christian Moreno, Marines, Marine Corps, Twentynine Palms, Bridgeport, combat, Twentynine, USMC, Combat Center
unit_name: Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center

transcript.text: (gentle music)
- My name is Tim Pasek.
I work for a company called Rigging for Rescue.
We're based out of Ouray, Colorado.
(uplifting music)
Yeah, we're brought in to come in and teach
the instructor cadre some more advanced rescue
and rope skills, so they have more depth of knowledge
and skill base, so they're more capable as instructors.
If there's an injury or something like that
at a training site, they're more ready to help the casualty.
(uplifting music)
- My name's David Charles Shuman.
I used to be an instructor here in 94, 95,
and so I'm kind of excited to come back.
And this is our second time out here working with MWTC.
And it's great that they already have a background in ropes.
They've already been through courses here,
because we can actually take it a little bit quicker,
and some more advanced moves that I wouldn't be able to do
maybe at another location with another organization.
(uplifting music)
- Staff Sergeant Aaron Buczek,
and I am the Staffing CIOC of Mount Engineer Cadre.
It's very intense as you can tell,
dealing with class five terrain.
It's essential to the Marine Corps.
So they're the subject matter experts
when it comes to rope rigging in order to vertically raise
or lower a patient off class five terrain.
So I've just expanded my toolbox,
in case a casualty was to occur on the mountain.
I'd have the skills and tools in order to get 'em to safety.
(uplifting music)
It's a rush, it's an adrenaline rush,
would be the first thing.
And then B, you run through your head
that everything that you've rigged,
as far as ropes and rescue goes is tied correctly,
'cause your life's on the line.
So it really hits home on how important
and how technical our rope skills are
up here at (mumbling).
(uplifting music)
